headline: session-continue.sh blocks a stop under 5 conditions, always by emitting decision:block JSON and never by exit 2: an armed continuation sentinel (:1334/:1336, capped by CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX), the mechanical 🔧 arm for this session's own uncommitted files (which feeds that same path; off with CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0), the ship floor on 📦 and 🚀 (:1199; off with CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0), and the wake floor (:895; off with CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0), and a kill phrase in the last user message disarms all of them.

session-continue.sh blocks a stop under 4 conditions. (1) An agent-set sentinel exists: blocked at lines 1334/1336, turned off only by `clear` or an operator kill phrase, and bounded by CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX. (2) The mechanical 🔧 arm finds this session's own uncommitted writes: it arms at line 1072 and blocks through lines 1334/1336; CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0 disables it. (3) The ship floor finds 📦/🚀 work that is this session's own: blocked at line 1199; CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0 disables it. (4) The wake floor finds no inbox watcher armed: blocked at line 895; CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0 disables it. The operator kill-switch phrases also stop all four.

In Stop mode, session-continue.sh blocks a stop under 5 conditions, each by printing {decision:"block"} at one of three places (lines 1334/1336, 1199 and 895); its exit-2 paths are only reachable in CLI modes. (1) An agent-set sentinel (lines 1334/1336) is stopped by a kill-switch phrase or the CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX cap. (2) The mechanical uncommitted-own-files arm (armed at 1072, blocks at 1334/1336) is turned off by CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0 or capped by CC_MECH_MAX. (3) and (4) The ship floor for committed-but-unlanded or landed-but-not-live work (line 1199) is turned off by CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0 or capped by CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX. (5) The wake floor for an unarmed inbox watcher (line 895) is turned off by CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0 or held back by CC_WAKE_FLOOR_MAX and CC_WAKE_FLOOR_TTL_S. A kill-switch phrase in the user's last message also stops every floor.

session-continue.sh blocks a stop under 5 conditions: (1) a sentinel the agent armed with `set` (block emitted at 1334/1336, capped by CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX); (2) the mechanical arm, for uncommitted files this session wrote while the rung is 🔧 (sentinel written at 1072, turned off by CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0 and CC_MECH_MAX); (3) the ship floor on 📦 and (4) the ship floor on 🚀 (both at 1199, turned off by CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0 and CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX); and (5) the wake floor (895, turned off by CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0, CC_WAKE_FLOOR_MAX and CC_WAKE_FLOOR_TTL_S). All five also stand down on an operator kill phrase.

session-continue.sh blocks a stop under 5 conditions, always as decision:block JSON with exit 0. (1) An agent-set sentinel (lines 1334/1336) stops blocking on a kill-switch phrase, on `clear`, or at the CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX cap. (2) A mechanically armed sentinel for this session's own uncommitted files (armed at 1072, blocks at 1334/1336) is turned off by CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0 or CC_MECH_MAX. (3) The ship floor for committed-but-unlanded work (📦, line 1199) and (4) the ship floor for landed-but-not-live work (🚀, line 1199) are turned off by CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0 or CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX. (5) The wake floor (line 895) is turned off by CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0, CC_WAKE_FLOOR_MAX or CC_WAKE_FLOOR_TTL_S. The operator kill-switch phrase disables all five.

The hook blocks a stop only by emitting {decision:"block"} and exiting 0, never by exit 2 in Stop mode. There are 4 conditions. (1) An agent-armed sentinel, emitted at lines 1336/1334, is stopped by `clear`, a sid mismatch or the CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX cap. (2) The mechanical 🔧 arm for this session's uncommitted writes arms at line 1072 and blocks at 1336/1334; CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0 or the CC_MECH_MAX budget stops it. (3) The ship floor for 📦/🚀 own work, at line 1199, is off with CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0 or once CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX is spent. (4) The wake floor for an unarmed inbox watcher, at lines 894-895, is off with CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0 or limited by CC_WAKE_FLOOR_MAX and CC_WAKE_FLOOR_TTL_S. An operator kill-switch phrase in the last user message overrides all four.

rotate-logs.sh has 7 real bugs; I found them by reading it and did not run it. The worst is that line 5 doesn't check whether cd worked, so line 11 can delete *.gz files in $HOME or another wrong directory. Next: line 11 keeps only keep-1 archives, line 8 gzip refuses when the archive name already exists, line 11's *.gz pattern deletes unrelated archives, line 7 skips files 1 to 2 days old, and lines 6 and 11 split file names that contain spaces.

rotate-logs.sh has 7 real bugs, worst first: an unchecked, unquoted `cd` that can make it delete .gz files in the wrong directory; gzip refusing to overwrite the existing .gz, so each log is only ever rotated once; the `tail -n +$keep` off-by-one that keeps only keep-1 archives; `-mtime +1` meaning 2 or more days; word-splitting on odd filenames; pruning of unrelated .gz files; and a success message printed even when steps fail.

rotate-logs.sh has 8 real bugs. The worst is the unchecked `cd $dir` (line 5): if it fails, line 11 deletes .gz files in the wrong directory (e.g. $HOME). Line 11 also deletes every *.gz, not just rotated logs, and keeps one archive fewer than asked. The others: a second rotation of the same log fails because the .gz name already exists, `-mtime +1` means 2 days rather than 1, filenames are split on spaces in both the loop and xargs, and keep is never checked while failures still exit 0.

By reading rotate-logs.sh without running it, I found 7 real bugs. The worst is on line 5: the script doesn't check that `cd $dir` worked and doesn't quote it, so line 11 can delete *.gz files in the wrong directory. Next come an off-by-one in `tail -n +$keep` that keeps one archive too few, an over-broad *.gz glob, xargs breaking on whitespace, looping over parsed `ls` output, `-mtime +1` meaning 2 or more days, and an unquoted `[ $(find ...) ]` test.

I found 6 real bugs by reading rotate-logs.sh (not running it). The worst: an unchecked, unquoted `cd` (line 5) can make line 11 delete *.gz files in the wrong directory. Next: line 11 keeps one archive too few (`tail -n +$keep` should use keep+1), and `xargs` splitting on spaces can delete the wrong files. Lower: `-mtime +1` skips logs 24-48 hours old, `$(ls)` breaks names with spaces, and gzip fails silently when the .gz already exists.

rotate-logs.sh has 6 real bugs. The worst: with no argument, or a directory that does not exist, it deletes *.gz files in $HOME or the caller's directory. Also: retention keeps one archive too few, a log can only be rotated once, -mtime +1 means 2 or more days, filenames with spaces break, and it deletes unrelated .gz files.

rotate-logs.sh has 9 real bugs. The worst is that `cd $dir` is never checked, so a missing or bad directory makes the script gzip and delete files in $HOME or wherever it was run from. Next: the prune deletes every .gz in the directory, `tail -n +$keep` keeps one archive too few, and archive names collide so each log rotates only once.

rotate-logs.sh has 7 real bugs; the worst are an unchecked cd that can rotate and delete files in the wrong directory, an off-by-one in tail that deletes one archive too many, and xargs splitting filenames so rm can delete the wrong files.
